grammar.title: Name the material used to make a work
grammar.formation: Noun + をもとに（して） + predicate; noun + をもとにした + noun.
grammar.explanation: をもとに identifies source material used in making or developing something. A film may be made from old photographs or an interview. The phrase does not say the result copies every detail unchanged. をもとにした modifies a following noun. に基づいて can overlap in some contexts; this lesson tests the stated source and attachment, not a universal ban on other source expressions.
grammar.example: 古い写真をもとに映像を作った。
grammar.translation: They made the video using old photographs as source material.

examples.ja: {古|ふる}い{写真|しゃしん}をもとに{映像|えいぞう}を{作|つく}った。
examples.en: They made the video using old photographs as source material.

examples.ja: これは{実話|じつわ}をもとにした{脚本|きゃくほん}だ。
examples.en: This is a script based on a true story.

examples.ja: {聞|き}き{取|と}りの{記録|きろく}をもとに、{構成|こうせい}を{考|かんが}える。
examples.en: We’ll plan the structure from the interview record.

grammar.mistake: Before a noun, use をもとにした, not をもとにする noun. The source phrase alone does not prove historical accuracy.

grammar.title: Read a channel or the extent of a period
grammar.formation: Noun + を通じて（つうじて） / を通して（とおして） + predicate.
grammar.explanation: These expressions can name a channel or intermediary, or describe an extent such as a whole period. レンを通じて asks or arranges something through Ren; 一年を通じて describes the whole year. Many contexts also accept を通して. Preferences depend on wording and register; do not force a contrast that the context cannot support. A named intermediary is different from the material used to make a film.
grammar.example: レンを通じて、店主に話を聞いた。
grammar.translation: They interviewed the shop owner through Ren.

examples.ja: レンを{通|つう}じて、{店主|てんしゅ}に{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.en: They interviewed the shop owner through Ren.

examples.ja: {一年|いちねん}を{通|つう}じて、{商店街|しょうてんがい}を{撮影|さつえい}した。
examples.en: They filmed the shopping street throughout the year.

examples.ja: {交流|こうりゅう}を{通|とお}して、{違|ちが}う{世代|せだい}の{人|ひと}と{知|し}り{合|あ}った。
examples.en: Through the exchange, I got to know people of a different generation.

grammar.mistake: The readings つうじて and とおして match different written verbs. Both may be grammatical with periods or means; identify the role rather than guessing a uniquely permitted variant.

grammar.title: Follow the issue around which views differ
grammar.formation: Noun + をめぐって / をめぐり + predicate; noun + をめぐる + noun.
grammar.explanation: In a report, をめぐって presents an issue around which discussion or differing views develop. Here the cinema site’s future use is the shared issue. をめぐる modifies a noun, as in 跡地をめぐる議論. This is more marked and formal than an ordinary friend’s について; it belongs in the meeting report, not in every casual question. Disagreement does not itself tell you which proposal won.
grammar.example: 跡地の使い方をめぐって、意見が分かれた。
grammar.translation: Opinions differed over how to use the former site.

examples.ja: {跡地|あとち}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}をめぐって、{意見|いけん}が{分|わ}かれた。
examples.en: Opinions differed over how to use the former site.

examples.ja: {再開発|さいかいはつ}をめぐる{議論|ぎろん}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.en: The debate over redevelopment is continuing.

examples.ja: {費用|ひよう}をめぐり、{二|ふた}つの{案|あん}を{比|くら}べた。
examples.en: They compared two proposals in a discussion centred on the cost.

grammar.mistake: Use をめぐる before 議論, not をめぐって議論 as a single noun modifier. A continuing discussion is not a completed decision.

grammar.title: Include a representative member of a wider group
grammar.formation: Noun + をはじめ（として） + clause; noun + をはじめとする + noun.
grammar.explanation: をはじめ names a prominent or representative member and includes others. 住民をはじめ、店主や学生も means residents as well as shop owners and students, not necessarily residents speaking first. をはじめとする connects to a following group noun. This phrase is common in formal speech and writing; this report lists who participated and then distinguishes their suggestions.
grammar.example: 住民をはじめ、店主や学生も参加した。
grammar.translation: Residents, as well as shop owners and students, took part.

examples.ja: {住民|じゅうみん}をはじめ、{店主|てんしゅ}や{学生|がくせい}も{参加|さんか}した。
examples.en: Residents, as well as shop owners and students, took part.

examples.ja: {資料館|しりょうかん}をはじめとする{施設|しせつ}が{協力|きょうりょく}した。
examples.en: Facilities including the local archive helped.

examples.ja: {子供|こども}をはじめ、{幅広|はばひろ}い{世代|せだい}が{映画|えいが}を{楽|たの}しんだ。
examples.en: Children and people from a wide range of generations enjoyed the film.

grammar.mistake: Do not infer chronological order from をはじめ. Before a noun use をはじめとする; before a clause をはじめ is possible.

dialogues.title: A familiar bakery in the documentary
dialogues.description: Two friends watch old photographs and hear the former owner’s story.

exercises.prompt: What material did the makers use for the video?
exercises.explain: Misaki reports 古い写真をもとに作った. The film uses those photographs as material.

exercises.prompt: How did they get to interview the former shop owner?
options: Through Ren, whose mother knew the owner
By asking Mori at the meeting
By reading only the sign outside
exercises.explain: Misaki says レンを通じて and then explains the introduction through his mother’s friend.

exercises.prompt: What occupies the old bakery’s location now?
exercises.explain: Misaki identifies the place as the bookshop now. The cinema belongs to another scene.

exercises.context: Complete the taught をもとに expression immediately before 脚本: “a script based on a true story.”
exercises.line: {実話|じつわ}をもとに＿＿{脚本|きゃくほん}です。
exercises.explain: をもとにした modifies 脚本. をもとにして connects to a predicate; をもとにする脚本 would assign a different active role to the script.

exercises.line: {交流|こうりゅう}を{通|とお}して、{知|し}り{合|あ}った。
exercises.prompt: Which reading is written in this expression?
exercises.explain: 通して is とおして; 通じて would be つうじて. This tests reading, not a false grammatical prohibition on the other expression.

exercises.line: {一年|いちねん}を{通|つう}じて、{商店街|しょうてんがい}を{撮影|さつえい}した。
exercises.prompt: What role does 一年 play here?
options: The whole period over which filming took place
The person who introduced the owner
The photographs used to make a script
exercises.explain: 一年を通じて gives a period extending throughout the year. It is not an intermediary.

exercises.prompt: How long is the film shown at the venue?
exercises.explain: The first paragraph says 十二分の記録映画. A year is only the period in a separate grammar example.

exercises.prompt: How were the dates of the photographs checked?
options: By assuming every memory supplies an exact date
By asking about the vacant cinema site
exercises.explain: 写真の日付は資料館の記録で確かめた states the check. Memories are labelled separately.

exercises.prompt: What does the owner’s recorded narration bring across?
options: Smells and sounds not visible in the photographs
A decision to build parking at the cinema
A newly completed script for a fictional comedy
exercises.explain: The second paragraph names 匂いや音. The narration evokes them; photographs cannot literally reproduce smells.

exercises.meaning: Constrained source statement: made this video using old photographs.
exercises.explain: The source is the photographs; the made work is this video.

exercises.prompt: What was decided about the site’s final use?
options: It must all become a park
exercises.explain: Yui asks whether it is undecided, and Mori confirms they only shared proposals.

People with children wanted parking; shop owners wanted a park
Both groups wanted a new cinema
exercises.explain: Yui explicitly assigns the park and parking requests to those two groups.

exercises.prompt: What is the stated next step?
options: Check the dimensions and discuss it again next month
exercises.explain: The dimensions and alley entrance will be checked; the next meeting is next month.

exercises.context: Use the taught をめぐる noun-modifier pattern immediately before 議論: “debate over redevelopment.”
exercises.line: {再開発|さいかいはつ}を＿＿{議論|ぎろん}が{続|つづ}いている。
exercises.explain: をめぐる modifies the noun 議論. The other two connect the issue to a predicate, rather than forming this noun modifier.

exercises.context: Complete the taught をはじめとする pattern before 世代: generations including children.
exercises.line: {子供|こども}をはじめと＿＿{幅広|はばひろ}い{世代|せだい}が{集|あつ}まった。
exercises.explain: をはじめとする links the representative member to the group noun here. として and としながら do not form this modifier. The related past modifier とした is also possible in appropriate contexts, so it is not used as a wrong option.

exercises.line: {住民|じゅうみん}をはじめ、{店主|てんしゅ}や{学生|がくせい}も{参加|さんか}した。
options: Residents took part, along with shop owners and students
exercises.explain: をはじめ includes other participants around the named representative group; it does not supply their speaking order.

options: Parking on the north side, with a park on the rest
Removing every tree for a new bookshop
exercises.explain: The third paragraph gives the north-side split as a proposal; its feasibility is still to be checked.

exercises.prompt: What does the report say about the cost?
options: It was asked about, but no specific amount was given
The report says every proposal is free
exercises.explain: 費用についても質問が出たが、具体的な金額は示されなかった. None of the proposals has an approved cost here.

exercises.prompt: How will people who could not attend be included?
options: They will receive the report and can submit views
They have already voted for the final plan
They can no longer give any view
exercises.explain: The final paragraph plans delivery of the report and receiving their opinions; no completed vote is stated.

exercises.meaning: Constrained continuing debate: discussion over the former site is still continuing.
exercises.explain: The noun modifier をめぐる attaches to 議論; まだ続いている does not say a plan has been approved.

recycling.reason: The remembered bakery, familiar sign and alley naturally retrieve 見覚え and 路地 from the recent narrative unit. A five-percent recent-reference target preserves a believable screening conversation and report handover without padding with unrelated personality or refusal vocabulary.

issue: をめぐって / をめぐる
watch.prompt: Optionally use a short report or documentary from your own material. Identify the material or speaker behind one claim, an issue under discussion, and one proposal or decision. Save only expressions that actually occur; do not infer a speaking order from a participant list.
